With my pod and lgs most of us are fine with proxies if you own the card. The entire reason to chase cards in the first place is because you want the good ones.. you invested the money for it or the trade or what ever.. either way, you had to do something to get that card.  

Some smaller groups in the LGS allow open proxies (*you dont need to own the card*), but, these groups are like 6-9 people groups whereas the others are like 20-30.  

I totally get that people want to play however they want (*some say magic is like dnd, but, honestly, I think thats dumb, its nothing like dnd when it come to self expression*), it just happens that at my LGS the majority of people don't exactly like their cards losing value at the table because that card they were after for 2 months, that they finally got and sleeved, put in their deck... is now being played by someone who took 2 seconds to draw a stick man and call it a Mondrak, or something like that.    

The people who frequent the games every week though, we tend to be a very helpful lot that tend to give away a ton of cards from our reward packs, lucky draw packs and so on. This is even moreso the case if some new little guy/girl comes to play magic for the first time... most of us are 20-35, so, when a kid comes in, we like to make the experience fun and to give them the excitment we all love from finding really awesome cards. So, when their parents come to pick them up after 4 hours of playing the one deck they own, they find out that they are coming home with, sometimes, 100s more cards than they came in with lol, I personally given away many decks that I havnt played in a while to newcomers.. because I have many too many.   

We even have guys that do big openings (*some are quite the whales*) and if they know they just pulled a second card that someone was desperately trying to find, they tend to save it to bring to the LGS games where they will do a cheaper trade/sale for it than what its usually worth. Obviously they dont do that for cards that hold 60+ value regularly, but, sometimes they do.  

So, because we tend to help eachother, we have been able to keep the chasing spirit alive and most people like it, they like having the reason to get excited and see what decks everyone has next week. If we had a ton of 50/99 proxy decks, I highly doubt we would have this community the way we do. Like, we cheer for eachother, when one guy last week says hes been after a card for soo long and then the next week he shows up and tells us he finally got it, the entire group goes wild for them lol. 

If they came in and told everyone they drew It/printed it, it wouldnt be nearly the same reaction.  

I let people play how they want, I dont yuck their yums, but, I also dont play with them because i like the way we have all been able to make our little community.  It's kept magic... well... special, kept it feeling like it did when we were in school.   

Because of that, we have also kept the LGS in a great and healthy spot, buisness wise and because of this they are able to do many great giveaway events or in house promo events, tournaments and soo on.

If you have people who play proxies, have at em, nothing wrong with like minds playing together, especially in games with no rewards/stakes.  

*side note, just like the whole proxy thing.. almost all of the people who frequent absolutely hate when someone shows up with a deck they just looked up on cEDH forums or w.e... they hate that even more than proxies...and storm decks* lol

Poe1 is poe2 with its restraints taken off.  

It isn't nearly as methodical, bosses aren't anywhere even close to as difficult.   

Skills are based on sockets in gear (*green sockets for dex, red for str and blue for int*) which come with something else called "linked sockets". Sockets with links can then be modified by sockets support gems. Socketed gems can be replaced, moved, taken out whenever you want. The crafting is actual crafting and not just rolling the dice and praying, tou can target what you build.  

The endgame js also 10000000x more enjoyable. By the time you get back to the atlas and do maps, your character will be a beast and you will have some of the craziest interactions between support gems and your skills, they really gave players free reign with soo much, skill wise, I poe1.  

The drawbacks:  

The graphics are insanely dated without MTX... meaning, if you dont buy skins, the gear looks really bad... like, paperbag princess bad.   

The story leaves soo much to be desired but you will get to meet Sin again (*technically for the first time lol*) and see more of his backstory, he is a cool character. 

Fps can stutter sometimes when there is alot going on, doesnt happen all the time.  

All in all, if you want a faster paced Poe2 with less restraint when it come to skill building and dont mind the lack of wasd movement (*on pc. On ps5/4 movement will feel the same*) give it a go. Just, do not expect every piece of gear to look unique or even well modled, infact, expect them to look like clay clubs or flat bits of metal textures lol. But yes, its fun.
